newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela says Placer Dome Ls Cristinas mine safe.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela says Placer Dome Ls Cristinas mine safe.

text.p: Canadian gold mining company Placer Dome Inc's rights to the joint venture Las Cristinas concession are secure despite a rival claim from Crystallex International Corp, a top government official said.

"We want to make clear to the international and Venezuelan audience that the transnational company, Crystallex, has no right whatsoever to these concessions," Elias Nadim Ynaty, president of state holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) was quoted as saying in a CVG release.

Crystallex has said it acquired blocks four and six of the Las Cristinas concession after buying local company Inversora Mael CA. But Ynaty said Inversora Mael gave up its rights to the blocks on October 17, 1991.
Placer Dome won a subsequent bidding round for a 70 percent stake to develop the concession with its partner CVG for a projected investment of more than $600 million.

"This is a problem which will be totally cleared up in the legal proceedings and based on that, we have total confidence in the future development of this gold project, which we have started with Placer Dome," he added.

Rival Canadian mining company Crystallex has taken its claim to the Supreme Court. Its lawyers say binding Supreme Court decisions in 1991 and 1996 found in its favor and the company recently took further action to establish ownership.
Ynaty said the Las Cristinas row was motivated by enemies of Placer Dome, "seeking to take advantage of the situation and make fun of the Venezuelan state."

The CVG chief's comments came in response to a call by the Venezuelan Mining Chamber earlier Wednesday for the government to clarify the ownership dispute over Las Cristinas, which is the most important Venezuela mining project in decades.
Roughly 80 percent of the estimated eight million ounces of recoverable gold at the Las Cristinas site are contained in the disputed blocks.
Government officials have consistently backed Placer Dome's rights to the gold concession in southeastern Venezuela since Crystallex took up its claim earlier this year.
